title.value: Environmental Risk of Psychiatric Disease: A Systematic Review on Air Pollution, Mental Health, and Frontolimbic Brain Regions
title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote: Environmental Risk of Psychiatric Disease: A Systematic Review on Air Pollution, Mental Health, and Frontolimbic Brain Regions

extractions.description: This systematic review investigates the effects of air pollution on mental health, specifically anxiety and depressive symptoms, and frontolimbic brain regions. It analyzes studies reporting the impact of air pollution on these outcomes.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper directly links environmental factors (air pollution) to mental health, indicating a focus on sustainable development's health and well-being aspects.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: The extant literature suggests that air pollution is associated with increased depression and anxiety symptoms and alterations in brain regions implicated in risk of psychopathology.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on the impact of air pollution.
primary_category.quote: Recent research suggests that air pollution can increase risk of psychopathology, including anxiety and depressive disorders.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper specifically investigates the impact of air pollution on mental health.
primary_sub_category.quote: We systematically reviewed the MEDLINE database in Sept. 2021, for original articles reporting effects of air pollution on 1) anxiety or depressive symptoms and 2) frontolimbic brain regions.

new_primary_category.justification: No new primary category is needed.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No new primary subcategory is needed.
